entries.markdown: Two new Notion MCP tools move content to Trash after the user confirms. `notion-delete-pages` moves up to 20 pages, and `notion-delete-databases` moves up to 20 databases with their rows. Both need the update content capability. Locked pages and databases can't be moved to Trash. To undo a deletion, use `notion-restore-pages` or restore the item from Trash in Notion. See [Supported tools](/guides/mcp/mcp-supported-tools.md).

entries.markdown: Four new Notion MCP tools change existing comments. `notion-update-comment` replaces the text of a comment the user wrote, and `notion-delete-comment` deletes one. `notion-set-discussion-resolved` resolves or reopens a discussion. `notion-set-comment-reaction` adds or removes the user's emoji reaction. The tools need a Business or Enterprise plan. Get comment and discussion IDs from `notion-get-comments` or `notion-create-comment`. See [Supported tools](/guides/mcp/mcp-supported-tools.md).

## Rate limits

The Notion API enforces two rate limits: a per-connection limit and a per-workspace limit. Some endpoints also have their own limit.

### Per-connection limit

Each connection has a fixed budget of requests per 60-second window, based on the workspace's plan:

| Workspace plan | Limit |
| :- | :- |
| Business and Enterprise | 600 requests per minute (an average of 10 per second) |
| All other plans | 180 requests per minute (an average of 3 per second) |

The budget can be spent at any pace within the window — spread out evenly or in a single burst. When a request exceeds this limit, the `Retry-After` value is the time until the window resets, so it is at most 60 seconds.

[Querying a data source](/reference/query-a-data-source.md) has a separate limit of about 3 requests per second per connection. A request over this limit returns an HTTP 429 response with a `Retry-After` header. The [JavaScript SDK waits](https://github.com/makenotion/notion-sdk-js#automatic-retries) for `Retry-After` and retries for you. If you call the REST API directly, see [Retry rate-limited requests](#retry-rate-limited-requests).

### Per-workspace limit

A separate limit is shared across all of the workspace's connections and scaled to the workspace's plan. Because it's shared, requests can be rate limited even when each individual connection is within its per-connection limit. `Retry-After` for this limit can be longer than a minute.
